failures.detail: The claim asserts Michelle 'has not experienced it herself, indicating an asymmetry' with David's direct motivation, but the only Michelle turn cited (michelle:0050) is a hedged hypothetical about future benefit and does not itself establish that she has never experienced reuse benefit. The turn that actually supports 'has not experienced it herself' (michelle:0024, 'I can't say that I've ever benefited from it') is not cited anywhere in the evidence list, so this specific sub-claim is not backed by the cited turns as required.

The insight treats David's barrier (protecting anonymity/honouring consent terms when depositing already-collected audio-visual data) and Michelle's example (a consent-form clause stating data will go to UK Data Service, which deters some prospective participants from taking part at all) as the same phenomenon ('consent-form restrictions as a barrier'). These are functionally different barriers — one is about safeguarding data post-collection, the other is about a chilling effect on recruitment/participation before data even exists — and collapsing them risks obscuring that Michelle's concrete example is not structurally equivalent to David's stated primary barrier.
